title: Experimental Guideline for Fast 4D STEM Experiments Applied to Beam-Sensitive Samples
content: High-resolution characterization of beam-sensitive materials with transmission electron microscopy presents significant challenges due to their low damage thresholds, the limited visibility of low-atomic-number atoms, and difficulties in structural interpretation. While high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) has been often used for its effective dose control using large-area illumination, scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) has become a viable choice due to low-dose imaging modes enabled by segmented detectors [1, 2], which also provide imaging modes with an easier interpretation of the sample’s structure at atomic level. The latest generation of direct electron pixelated detectors now supports 4D STEM at frame rates comparable to conventional STEM [3], enabling enhanced information retrieval through phase recovery techniques such as integrated center of mass (iCoM), parallax-corrected bright-field (BF) imaging, and ptychography [4].
